interface.title: CADET-Equations: Model Equation Generator
interface.field: Chemical/bioprocess engineering: packed-bed liquid chromatography and crystallization process modelling
interface.stage_of_work: Model formulation and documentation (before simulation, and when writing a manuscript)
interface.what_it_is_for: You pick or upload a chromatography-column or crystallizer model setup, and it writes out the governing equations in LaTeX, with assumptions, a symbol/unit table and literature references, which you can export as .tex, a CADET-Python template or a JSON config.

data.note: I built most models by hand from the sidebar, starting from the default Plug Flow model. I also uploaded GRM.json, CSTR.json and cry_CSTR_primaryGrowth.json from the test files. GRM_reqBnd.json was not uploaded. Downloads I got: model.tex, unit_operation.py and config.json.

features.name: Composable model configurator with live equation rendering
features.general: Build up a mathematical model by switching physical mechanisms on and off in cascading dropdowns. The equations, title and descriptive text update right away, and badges show which downstream solvers support the result.
features.specific: Sidebar dropdowns (axial dispersion → particles → binding → binding model → bulk reaction → reaction model) rebuild the LaTeX for the interstitial and particle mass balances. The title updates (e.g. 'General Rate Model with Langmuir binding with Mass Action Law type reactions'). Sub-component: solver-compatibility badges for CADET-Core / CADET-Process / CADET-Semi-Analytic, which change with the model (e.g. Core and Process supported, Semi-Analytic not, for GRM + Langmuir + Mass Action Law).
steps: Add axial dispersion
Add particles (new dependent options appear)
Add binding and choose a binding model (Linear/Langmuir/SMA/Arbitrary)
Add a bulk reaction and choose its kinetics (Mass Action Law/Michaelis Menten/Arbitrary)
Read the updated equations and title
Read the solver-support badges
serves_tasks: Build a transport model step by step by adding physical mechanisms

features.name: Assumptions and symbol-table toggles
features.general: Switches that show or hide the list of modelling assumptions and a table of every symbol with its description, dependence and unit, next to the derived equations.
features.specific: 'Show equation description', 'Show Model Assumptions' and 'Show symbol table' switches above the equations. Assumptions are grouped into general, specific, binding-model and reaction-model lists.
steps: Toggle Show Model Assumptions on and read the grouped lists
Toggle Show symbol table on
Change the model and see both update to match
serves_tasks: Inspect the assumptions and symbols behind the equations

features.name: Unit-system and naming-convention switcher
features.general: Change the unit system and the variable-naming convention of a symbolic model. Unit columns, conversion factors and the symbols in every equation are rewritten to match.
features.specific: 'Select unit system' (SI/Legacy/CGS) adds an 'SI Conversion' column, e.g. cm with factor 100. 'Select parameter format' (CADET/Legacy) renames c_i^b → c_i, c_i^p → c_{p,i}, c_i^s → q_i in the table and the equations.
steps: Open Select unit system and choose CGS
Check the new Unit and SI Conversion columns in the symbol table
Open Select parameter format and choose Legacy
Check the renamed symbols in the table and equations
serves_tasks: Match the units and symbol names used in a manuscript or simulation file

features.name: Configuration round-trip (upload JSON / generate and download JSON)
features.general: Save the whole interface state as a JSON file, preview it, and later upload it to restore every control in one go.
features.specific: 'Upload a configuration file' (JSON/H5) shows 'Uploaded configuration applied!' and sets all sidebar controls. 'Generate configuration file' shows a 'Current configuration' JSON preview and a 'Download Configuration (as json)' button.

Press Generate configuration file to preview the JSON
Press Download Configuration (as json)
serves_tasks: Load a previously saved model setup instead of configuring it by hand
Save the current setup to reload later
Open a particle population-balance model from a saved setup

features.name: Multi-format model export
features.general: Export the derived model as document source and as an executable code skeleton whose contents follow the configured model.
features.specific: 'Download .tex' gives model.tex (assumptions, align environments, bibliography). 'Download CADET-Python template (.py file)' gives unit_operation.py; its signature and contents depend on the model family: get_unit_operation(ncomp) returning UNIT_TYPE, particle_type_000 and reaction_bulk for the chromatography GRM, get_unit_operation(nbins) with ncomp = nbins+1 and a crystallization 'reaction' dict for the crystallization model. A 'Generate PDF' button is also present but could not run here (see not_done).
steps: Scroll below the References
Press Download .tex
Press Download CADET-Python template
serves_tasks: Get the equations as a typeset document source
Get a ready-to-edit simulation input skeleton

features.name: Per-particle-type configuration (particle-size distribution)
features.general: Set how many sub-populations there are with a number stepper, then give each one its own options in collapsible panels. The equations gain a sum over the sub-populations.
features.specific: In developer mode, the 'Number of particle types' stepper (−/+) creates 'Particle type 1..N' expanders, each with Spatial resolution, impenetrable core-shell, side-cavities, Film diffusion kinetics mode and Geometry. The model becomes 'General Rate Model with particle-size distribution' with volume fractions d_j.
steps: Turn on Developer mode and choose Chromatography
Press + on Number of particle types
Expand a Particle type panel
Set its geometry, resolution and core-shell/side-cavity options
Read the summed flux term and the d_j constraint in the equations
serves_tasks: Describe a mixture of particle sizes

features.name: Population-balance mechanism builder
features.general: Behind a switch that exposes less-tested model families, build a population-balance model by choosing the reactor type and switching birth/death mechanisms on and off (nucleation and growth, aggregation, fragmentation). Each mechanism adds its source terms, kernel options and symbols.
features.specific: Developer mode exposes a Model Family selector; the Crystallization family offers Reactor type (CSTR/DPFR), Primary particle formation with Size-dependent growth / growth dispersion / secondary nucleation, Aggregation with an Aggregation kernel picker, and Fragmentation. These add B_agg − D_agg and B_frag − D_frag to the PBE, and DPFR adds Danckwerts boundary conditions.
steps: Turn on Developer mode and pick Model Family Crystallization
Choose Reactor type CSTR or DPFR
Turn Aggregation on (kernel picker appears)
Turn Fragmentation on
Read the updated PBE, solute balance and symbol table
serves_tasks: Add particle-interaction mechanisms and change the reactor type
Open a particle population-balance model from a saved setup

not_done: Generate PDF does not work on this server: pdflatex is not installed, so the error is a missing-dependency problem, not a broken feature. After the error the script stopped, and the 'Generate configuration file' button stayed missing until another control re-ran the page; I changed the unit system back to SI only to force that rerun (screens/034.webp). This recovery step was removed from the save-configuration task.
Uploading GRM_reqBnd.json: my click didn't open the file picker (the sidebar wasn't scrolled back to the uploader), and I stopped to stay within about 100 actions.

Did not open the other dropdown options (Column geometry, Column resolution, Binding kinetics mode, Film diffusion mode, surface diffusion, Aggregation kernel types, Size-dependent growth, secondary nucleation, Number of components) or the core-shell/side-cavity switches, so I can't say what they change.

My own .tex and template downloads were of the chromatography GRM; the replay downloaded them for the crystallization DPFR model (model.tex 6219 bytes; unit_operation.py with get_unit_operation(nbins=50)), shown in check/screens/019.webp.
The only screen cited for the .tex and template downloads (screens/031.webp) shows the download buttons, not the files; their contents come from reading the downloads.
Did not open or check the downloaded config.json; its contents were only seen in the on-page preview (screens/036.webp).

Observed quirks: (1) while a config file stays in the uploader it is re-applied on every rerun, overriding manual edits: setting Aggregation to Yes with cry_CSTR_primaryGrowth.json still attached snapped back to No (screens/043.webp, screens/044.webp), and I had to remove the file (x) first (screens/045.webp); in the replay one Aggregation=Yes reverted even after removal and had to be set again. These recovery steps were removed from the aggregation/fragmentation task. (2) Changing Advanced options reset Add particles (and, in the replay, Add binding) to No. (3) Uploading GRM.json kept the earlier Mass Action Law reaction from the previous state. (4) The Legacy format shows unrendered red '\b' in bulk-reaction symbols (screens/025.webp, screens/027.webp). (5) In the replay, core-shell=Yes set in Particle type 2 reverted to No after a later rerun.
